original_test_intent: Reload the selected BMC watchdog timer through the out-of-band Reset Watchdog Timer command and verify the intended countdown/control effect without changing the configured watchdog policy or causing an unintended host action.
original_method: Master raw 0x06/0x22 is preserved. The DeepSeek `mc watchdog reset` wrapper is acceptable only when its implementation and target are verified to issue that exact command and post-state is read back.
manual_activity: Owner identifies the watchdog consumer and safety role, approves one reset in a maintenance window, and decides whether the observed timer reload and host behavior satisfy the project plan.
required_inputs: Verified BMC and associated host identity
Project-approved expected reload behavior and tolerance
Maintenance window and explicit one-shot approval
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, dmesg or syslog
Capture current watchdog state before reset
Do not reset an unknown or safety-critical watchdog
Use raw 0x06/0x22 or a proven equivalent wrapper exactly once
Do not set, disable or reconfigure watchdog policy
Do not auto-retry after failure or ambiguous state
Stop on target mismatch, unknown action or unavailable recovery
agent_execution_scope: Verify BMC-host association and protected session
Read watchdog use/action/timeout/countdown and host workload state
Present the exact one-shot reset for approval
Issue the approved Reset Watchdog Timer request once
Immediately read back timer state and monitor host/BMC reachability
Preserve command completion, timing and existing logs
engineer_actions: Approve target, watchdog policy interpretation and maintenance window
Confirm resetting the timer will not mask a fault or defeat a safety mechanism
Own any later watchdog restoration or fault response

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `ipmitool mc watchdog reset` is a plausible wrapper for raw 0x06/0x22, but output alone cannot prove correct timer ownership, reload behavior or absence of an unintended watchdog action.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After read-only prechecks and explicit OK, issue one protected `ipmitool ... raw 0x06 0x22` or verified equivalent wrapper, then use the separate Get Watchdog Timer path for immediate readback.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source one-command scope and 10/5 timing metadata remain unchanged; no loop or retry is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Prefer the exact raw request or a version-pinned wrapper whose raw equivalence is demonstrated, with before/after countdown evidence and independent host/BMC monitoring.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds watchdog-owner/policy discovery, explicit approval, timer readback, recovery readiness and evidence preservation while rejecting the source log-clearing step.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A Get Watchdog Timer read supplies pre/post evidence but does not replace the required reset; a Set Watchdog Timer operation is out of scope.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A reset can postpone an intended fault response or race an imminent expiry; command completion without timer readback can falsely appear successful.

project_override_considerations: A PA Manager or vendor watchdog action may be used only if the approved version exposes the selected BMC/host, exact Reset Watchdog Timer semantics, one-shot execution and raw/post-state evidence; any policy change is separate coverage.
expected_evidence: Verified BMC-host identity and protected-session metadata
Pre-reset watchdog use/action/pre-timeout/timeout/countdown and host workload state
Explicit approval and exact raw/wrapper command mapping
Redacted request/response, completion code and timestamps
Immediate post-reset countdown/state proving the intended reload
Host power/boot and BMC reachability observation
Preserved SEL, dmesg and syslog with no configuration change or retry

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The raw 0x06/0x22 Master command and DeepSeek wrapper describe the same intended reset. The source acceptance is under-specified and its log-clearing step is unsafe, but no two normative reset intents contradict each other.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Reset semantics are identifiable. Watchdog ownership, active policy, approval and recovery are project execution-readiness inputs; execution stops if they cannot be resolved.

review_improvement: Turns an output-only wrapper suggestion into a one-shot, policy-aware reset contract with exact raw coverage, pre/post countdown proof, preserved logs and independent recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: Reset Watchdog Timer reloads an existing countdown rather than configuring the watchdog. Its safety depends on who owns that watchdog and what expiry action is armed: reloading it can prevent an expected recovery action, while issuing it near expiry can race a host reset. Therefore the review requires pre-state ownership/action evidence and post-reset countdown proof, not merely a zero command exit.
